title: Colors and Describing Things
summary: Learn basic English color words. Practice using colors to describe everyday objects.

sections.p: Colors help us describe the world around us. In English, we use the verb 'to be' with colors. For example, we say 'It is red' or 'The pen is blue'. Color words usually go before nouns, like 'a red car', or after the verb 'is', like 'The car is red'.

ex.mean: The fruit has a red color.
The sky has a blue color.

sections.p: To ask about the color of something, we use the question 'What color is...?'. The answer usually starts with 'It is' or 'They are' followed by the color word. This is very useful when shopping or looking for your things.

ex.mean: Asking about the color of a car.
The car has a black color.
Asking about the color of shoes.

sections.p: When we talk about more than one thing, we change 'is' to 'are'. We say 'The cats are white' or 'The books are green'. The color word stays the same even if there are many things.

ex.mean: More than one flower is yellow.
More than one pen is green.

tip: Look around your room right now. Say the color of three things out loud in English, like 'The door is brown.'

quiz.en: The grass is green. -> Grass is ___.
